To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the upper region on ‘Robusta 3’ contains multiple genes contributing fire blight resistance.

we identified markers derived form putative resistance genes associated with a broad, large-effect QTL for resistance to fire blight in Malus ‘Robsuta 5’, a cultivar widely used as a rootstock and a scion.
we have identified markers derived from genes associated with a QTL for fire blight on linkage group 2 of ‘Robusta5’.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of markers associated with quantitative resistance to fire blight in apple.
the development of molecular markers for the detection of genetic resistance to fire blight in apple.
the identification of genes that are associated with fire blights resistance in Malus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ‘Robusta 3’ region is the most important QTL for fire blight disease resistance, but that other regions of the apple genome are also important and may be involved in resistance to other strains of E. amylovor.

the fire blight resistance of ‘Robusta5′ is polygenic and that the QTL detected on LG3 of ‘Robusta′5′ is not a single gene but rather a complex locus with multiple genes contributing to the resistance.

the fire blight resistance of ‘Robusta5’, as well as the resistance of the progenies used in this study, is controlled by multiple loci on linkage groups 3 and 7, and the resistance is not completely stable and is dependent on the pathogenicity of E.amylovorae strains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a set of candidate markers for fire blight disease resistance that can be applied to breeding programmes for the improvement of fire blight disease resistant apple cultivars.
fire blight resistance is a quantitative trait controlled by multiple genes.
the MxdRLP gene is a good candidate gene for fire blight disease resistance in apple.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many genes involved in fire blight resistance that can be used to breed fire blight resistance into apple.
the use of multiple E. amylovorainoculation strains is essential to detect QTLs and identify markers that are consistently associated with resistance.

the fire blight resistance QTL on LG3 of ‘Robusta’ is not a single gene, but rather contains several different genes, and that the relative contribution of each gene may vary depending on the pathogen isolate and other factors.
